seo.metaDescription: A column of dots for each period, where one dot is a fixed unit. The largest column is solid and carries a pill, and periods can be grouped.

props.markdown: A total for each period, counted in dots. Every period is a column, and each dot in it stands for the same unit, so the height of a column is how many units the period holds.

Use `WaffleColumns` for a sum per period where the size of each period should read as a count of things: signups per week, claims per month, dollars lost per week. `unit` sets the value of a dot and `wide` the dots across a column. The largest column is solid and the others soft (`peak={false}` makes them all solid), and a pill above it names the peak (`callout`). `group` labels runs of periods under their columns, such as the month, and `groupTone` picks a tone for each group.

If you want to see the individual items rather than a total, use [DotHistogram](/docs/dot-histogram): one dot per item, stacked by value. To compare several measures of the same items, use [StripPlot](/docs/strip-plot): one row of dots per measure.
Weeks in two months. `group` names the month under its columns and the default `callout` pins “Peak” above the biggest week. Every prop is serializable.
`groupTone` is a function that picks the tone of each group, here the last quarter, and `callout` returns your own pill segments. Functions in the props make this a client component.

`WaffleColumns` is built on `Chart`, so it follows the same keyboard model as the other charts: it is a single tab stop, and tabbing in shows the first column with its tooltip and announces it. The points are the periods, in one dimension: `←` and `→` move to the previous or next period. `Home` and `End` jump to the first and last point, `Enter` or `Space` selects the active point when the chart has `onSelect`, and `Esc` clears the active point. `Esc` is only consumed when a point is active, so an enclosing dialog still closes. The widget’s description ends with a keyboard hint (“Use arrow keys to move between points, Home and End for first and last, Escape to clear.”, plus “Press Enter to select.” with `onSelect`); `keyboardHint` replaces it, for example to translate it, and `keyboardHint=""` turns it off.

Screen readers get the chart title and description, then an announcement for each period the keyboard moves to, in the form “1 of 8, Aug 3, $9.8K”: its position, the period and its value. A visually hidden data table follows the chart with the columns Period and Value (named after the `x` and `y` fields when they are strings) and a Group column when `group` is set. `dataTable` renames the caption and headers, or turns it off.

The soft dots of columns that are not the peak are decorative and carry no meaning of their own, and the `callout` pill is `aria-hidden`, so it says nothing to a screen reader. Put the same facts in the `title`, the `description` or the data, as both examples do with the peak.
The full model is in the [accessibility guide](https://github.com/mwadon/tally-charts/blob/main/docs/a11y.md).
